Interoperability with priogrid and peacesciencer

Source: vignettes/interoperability.Rmd
interoperability.Rmd

ucdpR uses the identifiers native to two established peace-science tools: pgid for the released priogrid package and gwcode/ccode plus year for peacesciencer. The bridges preserve UCDP provenance and keep consequential matching and aggregation decisions explicit.

Year-sensitive country codes

State systems change over time, so country codes should not be translated with an ahistorical lookup table. ucdp_country_crosswalk() matches on both code and year. It normally asks peacesciencer to construct the mapping; a frozen crosswalk can be supplied for an offline replication.

library(ucdpR)

country_year <- data.frame(
  country_id = c(2, 20, 2),
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021),
  n_events = c(3, 1, 4)
)

frozen_codes <- data.frame(
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021),
  gwcode = c(2, 20, 2),
  ccode = c(2, 20, 2)
)

ucdp_country_crosswalk(
  country_year,
  from = "gw",
  code = "country_id",
  crosswalk = frozen_codes
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   country_id  year n_events ccode
#>        <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1          2  2020        3     2
#> 2         20  2020        1    20
#> 3          2  2021        4     2

Choose unmatched = "warn" or "error" during quality control. The returned ucdp_crosswalk attribute records match counts and the mapping source.

peacesciencer

ucdp_to_peacesciencer() renames or converts identifiers and calls peacesciencer::declare_attributes(). Input must already be unique at the requested unit. For event data, aggregate first:

state_year <- ucdp_aggregate(ged, unit = "country-year")

ps_state_year <- ucdp_to_peacesciencer(
  state_year,
  type = "state-year",
  system = "gw",
  code = "country_id"
)

# peacesciencer functions can now recognize the data type and state system
ps_state_year <- peacesciencer::add_nmc(ps_state_year)

Dyad-year data use code and code2 and become gwcode1/gwcode2 or ccode1/ccode2. If from and system differ, supply a frozen crosswalk or allow peacesciencer to build the year-specific conversion.

priogrid

Install the released priogrid package according to its website. It is not a hard dependency of ucdpR.

renv::install("prio-data/priogrid")

ged_pg <- ucdp_to_priogrid(ged)
grid_year <- ucdp_aggregate(ged_pg, unit = "grid-year", id = "pgid")

By default, ucdp_to_priogrid() extracts identifiers from priogrid::prio_blank_grid(), respecting its current configuration. For a frozen analysis, save that one-layer SpatRaster and pass it as grid. This also makes the analysis independent of later changes to package defaults.

Coordinates outside the grid or missing coordinates produce NA by default. Use missing = "drop" or "error" to make a different policy explicit.

The bridge returns the conventional pgid column rather than a private class. That keeps it directly usable with priogrid tables today and leaves a stable interface for the planned priogridR package later.
